Hypoxaemia - is abnormally low oxygen partial pressure in the arterial circulation. It is generally considered to be a partial pressure of less than 60mmHg which in a normal person would correspond to saturation’s of approx. 92% in a healthy patient 

Regulation of respiration: 

Under normal circumstances control of respiration is primarily under hypercapnic drive.

In hypoxaemia hypoxic drive is activated → increase in minute ventilation

![](/content/exams/anzca/2018/A/11/standard-image35.png){fig-alt="Respiratory control feedback loop linking sensors, central controller and muscles of respiration"}

- Peripheral chemoreceptors 
  - Located in the carotid body (innervated by CNIX) and Aortic Arch (innervated by CNX)
  - Stimulated in normal circumstances by decrease in PaO2  (under60mmHg) and inc PaCO2 
- Central Chemoreceptors
  - Located in Ventral Medulla 
  - Stimulated indirectly by increase in CO2, not sensitive to O2 so minimal contribution to hypoxaemia
  - Indirect mechanism: 
    - CO2 diffuses through BBB 
    - Increase ofCO2 in CSF - CO2+H20 (+ Carbonic Anhydrase)→  H2CO3 → HCO3- + H+
    - Fall in pH respiratory centre   

 Response to hypoxaemia:

- In Hypoxaemia hypoxic drive acts for rapid increase in MV 
- Synergistic increase in MV if PaCO2 is also increased 

![](/content/exams/anzca/2018/A/11/standard-image36.png){fig-alt="Minute ventilation against arterial oxygen tension with carbon dioxide and anaesthetic concentration curves"}

Respiratory response is triphasic:

1)  Initial rapid increase in MV
2)  MV Decline to new higher plateau MV
3)  If ongoing isocapnoea → slow ongoing rise in MV over hours 

Effect of General Anaesthesia 

- All anaesthetic agents depress the response to hypoxaemia 
  - 0.1 MAC 50-70 Depression of response 
  - 1.1 MAC 100% Depression of response
  - Residual Anaesthetic agent can impair ventilators drive to Hypoxaemia and Hypercapnia and need appropriate monitoring and supplemental O2 in recovery 

Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction

- Occurs primarily in response to low PAO2 
- Biphasic Response
  - Rapid Vasoconstriction of small vessels within minutes
  - Plateau at 5 min 
  - Second phase at around 40min
  - Max effect at 2-4hours
- Mechanism poorly understood 
- Results in: 
  - improved VQ matching
  - increased PVR
  - Volatile agents thought to have a dose dependant suppression of HPV, at 1 MAC approx. 20% inhibition OG HPV response
